note: FiveThirtyEight Elo through 2014-15, the lake's own Elo from 2015-16 (elo_source), computed with FiveThirtyEight's method from their 2013-14 closing ratings. It reproduces their 2014-15 within 2 points. Its fixed 100-point home edge predicts home teams win 62 percent, and they won 55 to 59 percent from 2015-16, so elo_win_prob is overconfident: teams given 86 percent won 81. elo_fit_* from 2014-15 fits the home edge to the previous three seasons and is calibrated within one point. Preseason and all-star games carry none.
True for the 172 games of the 2020 Orlando bubble, which ESPN marks as home games.
Holds preseason, all-star, play-in, and nba-cup games beside regular and playoffs. Filter season_type.
nba-cup is only the NBA Cup final, which does not count in the standings. Every other Cup game is regular.

NULL on NBA Stats rows from 1996-97 through 2000-01, and from 2001-02 to 2016-17 where ESPN's game roster does not list five starters for the team, about 1.4 percent of team games. started_source says whether NBA Stats or ESPN set it. ESPN rows for 1993-94 to 1995-96 carry it.
Rows for players who did not play carry 0 in every stat on NBA Stats rows, not NULL. Filter played before averaging or counting games.
About 2,100 ESPN rows have no player_id because the ESPN name did not resolve. Team totals still include them.
A traded player has a row per team plus a total row with multi_team true and no team_id. Use the total row for a season figure, never both.
Each season has a modern and a historical RAPTOR row per player. Filter model before averaging.
Points run about 1.5 per team-game under the box score before 2017-18. Rates from possessions read low in those seasons.
About 9,900 of 6.3M shots have coordinates outside the court, including heaves and bad source rows. Bound x_feet and y_feet for charts.
No season_type column. season_type_id 2 is regular, 4 playoffs, 5 play-in, 6 nba-cup. Join nba.games for the name.
Negative means the home team is favored. Lines start in 2006-07 and several books can quote one game, so pick a source and book or take the median.
A filler 2.5 with game_spread_available false before 2012-13. Use nba.game_lines.
Rows exist from 1996-97 but every tracking value before 2013-14 is zero. Only games, wins, losses, and minutes are real.
Rows exist from 1996-97 but every tracking value before 2013-14 is zero. Only games, wins, losses, and minutes are real.
Last Two Minute reports grade only the final two minutes of games within three points, plus overtime, from 2014-15.
Each block and steal is also its own row with an empty action_type and the action_number of the miss or turnover. Count block_player_id and steal_player_id, which sit on the primary row only.
NULL before 2005-06. The source did not record who was fouled.

NULL from 2026-27 on and in preseason, all-star, play-in, and nba-cup games, which neither the v2 source nor cdn.nba.com covers. 2025-26 comes from cdn.nba.com. fouled_player_id is NULL there too. Blocks and steals are complete.

qualifiers, fast_break, second_chance, from_turnover, points_in_paint, descriptor, official_id, and wall_clock come from cdn.nba.com and are NULL outside 2020-21 to 2025-26 regular seasons and playoffs, and on block and steal rows.
One row per player season on the player's last team, so a traded player's whole season sits under that team. Curated season tables name it last_team_id.
The team the player ended the season with. A traded player has one row for his whole season under it, and team_count says how many teams he played for. Use nba.player_box for games by team.
The team the player ended the season with. A traded player has one row for his whole season under it.

The team the player ended the season with. A traded player has one row per band for his whole season under it.
Games with at least one attempt in that band, not games played. gp is games played.
Attempts with no tracked defender fall in no band, so the four bands can sum to a little under the season's fga.
sportsdataverse's single-season ridge RAPM from stats.nba.com play-by-play and rotations, built by hoopR-nba-stats-data. o_rapm and d_rapm split it. The playoff rows rest on about 15 games a team.

RAPM with a prior: the previous season's possession-weighted regular season and playoff SPM, and for playoffs that season's regular season SPM. The first season of each sportsdataverse run has no prior.
A box-score SPM fitted to RAPM once per regular season and reused for playoffs, so playoff values are on the same scale but directional.
sportsdataverse's reimplementation of BPM 2.0 from box logs and listed positions. It will not match Basketball-Reference's published BPM exactly.
WAR on the RAPM rating with points per win fitted each regular season from team game logs and a replacement level of -2.0 per 100.

sportsdataverse's Kalman forecast in the style of DARKO, not the published DARKO. It projects the NEXT season, both season types carry the same value, and it is NULL until its panel spans two seasons.
The team the player played the most games for that season. teams lists every team, most games first.

Great-circle kilometers from the previous competitive game of the season. A game is placed at the ESPN venue for neutral sites, else at the home team's season arena as Basketball-Reference lists it, so a team that split a season between arenas is placed at the listed one. NULL for the first game of a season and where the arena is unknown: Seattle 1978-79 to 1984-85, Golden Hall and Tulane Gym in the ABA, and neutral sites before 1993-94.

A completed game newer than every NBA Stats game has source espn and game_id 'espn' plus its ESPN id. When NBA Stats publishes the game the row takes the NBA Stats id, and nba.game_xref maps the old id (source minted) to it. Its boxes come from ESPN and carry no plus_minus or team minutes, and play-by-play is in pbp_espn only.

One row per player ESPN lists as injured in each daily snapshot from 2026-09-08. A player missing from a snapshot was not listed that day. nba.injuries_latest is the newest snapshot. reported_at is UTC. player_id is NULL for players who have not yet played an NBA game, mostly rookies, and espn_athlete_id and player_name are always set.

ESPN's depth chart in each daily snapshot from 2026-09-08. depth_rank 1 is the starter at the position, and one player can hold several positions. nba.depth_charts_latest is the newest snapshot. player_id is NULL for players who have not yet played an NBA game, mostly rookies, and espn_athlete_id and player_name are always set.

Left out because their playoff games do not form an elimination bracket: 1954 opened with a round robin, and in 1948, 1956, and 1957 two teams played a tiebreaker game and then a series, which cannot be told apart by pairing teams.

Inferred from the winner's wins. In the latest season a round's format is taken from the previous season, so a series is decided once a team reaches that many wins, and winner_team_id is NULL until then.

Assumes the home-court team hosts (best_of + 1) / 2 games and that games are independent. It uses elo_pre, whose fixed 100-point home edge is overconfident from 2015-16, and home_court_series_prob_fit uses the fitted Elo and edge from 2014-15.
Regular season only, like every bref.player_* table. Playoff player totals exist only from 1993-94, summed from nba.player_box, and no table holds them earlier.

Ten regular-season games have no box in any source: 199311050UTA, 199401030UTA, 199401270WSB, 199402260CLE, 199404070UTA, 199601270WSB, 199602070UTA, 199603240CLE, 199603290UTA, and 199604050CHH. ESPN lists them in its schedule but published no box, and no other source covers 1993-94 to 1995-96. nba.box_reconciliation lists them with team_box_missing.
On a coach's technical foul or ejection, player_id is the coach's NBA Stats id, which is not in nba.players. About 4,000 events from 1996-97 to 2014-15.
